githubDelivery.rule: After each validated, reviewable, and reversible round checkpoint, commit the scoped work and push the current feature branch to the configured SEIS GitHub remote; verify the remote reference when the environment permits.
githubDelivery.externalBlockerHandling: Record network, approval, or platform limits honestly and retry only after a new explicit user delivery instruction or restored environment.

afterProgram.rule: Each 100-step wave is planned only after the prior wave has current validation evidence, a scope review, and an explicit risk review.

rounds.name: Program and UI-state foundation
rounds.objective: Record the 30-step cadence and build the first non-duplicative public UI-state audit.

rounds.name: Public package integration
rounds.objective: Connect the UI-state audit to source evidence, marketplace, catalog, and release contracts.

rounds.name: Evidence and regression validation
rounds.objective: Run focused and portfolio-level checks across public distribution, permissions, and application behavior.

rounds.name: Second evidence-backed capability
rounds.objective: Select and build a second non-duplicative public plugin only after an audited scope decision.

rounds.name: Release-quality handoff
rounds.objective: Run full regression, reconcile documentation, prepare commits, attempt approved delivery, and create the next-wave decision record.

steps.title: Record the 30-step program
Verify branch, remote delta, and no-personal boundary
Inventory non-duplicative public plugin gaps
Specify UI-state audit scope and non-goals
Create the public UI-state audit package
Add positive and negative static audit fixtures
Generate UI-state evidence
Register only in the public SEIS Repo marketplace
Refresh application catalog counts and fallback metadata
Bind integration and source-manifest contracts
Refresh release train and change evidence
Validate the plugin package structure
Run focused UI-state unit and MCP tests
Run application source, catalog, and matrix checks
Run public marketplace, install-state, and runtime checks
Run public lifecycle, fresh-task, and provenance checks
Run AI Core integration and requested-plugin coverage
Run Command Center and baseline SEIS checks
Audit the next public plugin gap
Record second plugin scope, non-goals, and safety boundary
Implement the second public plugin package
Add second plugin generator, evidence, and tests
Connect second plugin to marketplace, catalog, and integration
Validate second plugin release evidence
Run full public plugin regression and permission checks
Reconcile registry, documentation, and project manifest counts
Inspect diff, secret-safe boundary, and worktree
Prepare review-focused local commit sequence
Deliver every validated checkpoint to the current GitHub feature branch and verify remote ref
Publish program report and plan five 100-step waves

nextWaves.entryCriteria: All 30 initial steps had current evidence, the user requested continuation, and the completed Wave 1 scope and risk review selected bounded public source work.
Wave 1 has current validation, a completed repository-local handoff, a fresh scope and risk review, and explicit user authority to continue public SEIS Repo work on the current feature branch.
nextWaves.activationRule: Wave 2 completed only evidence-backed, public, repository-local steps; personal marketplace access, protected-branch writes, external release claims, and live provider activity remained outside scope.

nextWaves.entryCriteria: Wave 2 has current validation, a completed repository-local handoff, a fresh scope review, a risk review, and continued user authority to plan public SEIS Repo work.
nextWaves.activationRule: Wave 3 starts with discovery and a non-duplicative capability decision; it cannot add a public card, access the personal marketplace, write externally, use secrets, claim a release, or assert a live provider, deployment, or native runtime without separate current evidence and authorization.

nextWaves.entryCriteria: Wave 3 has current evidence and a scope review.
Wave 4 has current evidence and a scope review.
